{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABgQsnvg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhJtrfA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 164, "title": "Group display controls under the game and make Fullscreen focus on gameplay", "body": "## Problem

The browser UI currently separates **Scale / Display** into the top-right header while the rest of the player controls (Play/Pause, Reset, mute/volume and Fullscreen) live below the video. The display choices feel disconnected from the game they affect.

Worse, the current Fullscreen button calls `document.documentElement.requestFullscreen()`, making **the entire page** fullscreen (header, Help/GitHub, settings, cartridge picker and controls). Users reasonably expect **the game itself to become fullscreen**. On phones, however, a game-image-only fullscreen would hide the 12-button on-screen controller and make the emulator unplayable.

This Issue combines two directly related **player layout** improvements. Latest baseline inspected: `main` commit `58ac711b1d449e7b0d912645d58fdebf3ee7b6c3` (merged [PR #163](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/163)). See [`web/index.html`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/index.html), [`web/style.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/style.css), [`web/app.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/web/app.js).

## Desired behavior

### 1. Group display settings with playback tools

- Move the existing **Scale** and **Display (CRT / Pixel)** selectors from the header to the controls immediately beneath the game screen, near **Play/Pause, Reset, mute/volume and Fullscreen**.
- The header should stay light: **snes-rust**, Help and GitHub. Avoid extra top-right settings or duplicating display controls elsewhere.
- Both selectors remain **directly visible**, not hidden in Help, a gear menu or a popover.
- Group related controls by spacing/alignment rather than adding explanation text, boxes or a new settings panel. A small secondary row within the same control area is fine where the viewport is narrow. The visual focus remains on the emulator screen.
- Preserve the present behavior: Scale controls the existing canvas scaling, CRT remains the default for new users, Pixel/CRT can be switched live, explicit display preference persists, and the Pixel fallback continues to work if WebGL fails.
- Do not let controls shrink the game screen unnecessarily or cause overlap/horizontal scrolling on phones.

### 2. Make Fullscreen mean fullscreen *gameplay*, not fullscreen webpage

- Stop fullscreening `document.documentElement`. Request fullscreen on a **purpose-built game presentation element** so the page header, GitHub/Help, cartridge picker, unrelated text and ordinary webpage chrome do not appear.
- On **desktop / hardware-keyboard or gamepad-oriented layouts**, fullscreen should prioritize **only the emulated game image**, maximized within the screen, with **correct source aspect ratio** and neutral letterboxing/pillarboxing. Do not stretch pixels, crop content or change emulated framebuffer dimensions. The existing Pixel and CRT visuals must both render correctly at fullscreen size.
- On **touch phone/tablet layouts**, fullscreen must include the **game image and all 12 on-screen SNES controls** (D-pad directions, A/B/X/Y, L/R, Start/Select); otherwise the game is unplayable. In portrait, put controls below the game screen. In short landscape, put them to the left and right of the center image. Do not overlay controls on the game picture, clip them at screen/safe-area edges or require scrolling to reach core gameplay buttons.
- Provide a clearly discoverable **Exit fullscreen** action inside the fullscreen presentation on touch devices, where there is no Escape key. On desktop, Escape and/or a compact exit affordance should work. Keep the normal Fullscreen toolbar control for entering fullscreen and correct exit state, but do not leave the full regular toolbar visibly occupying the fullscreen game area.
- Keep game execution and user-selected Play/Pause state unchanged when entering and leaving. Fullscreen changes must not reset or reload the current cartridge, clear SRAM, change volume, toggle CRT/Pixel, or auto-pause.
- Design correctly for the Fullscreen API's element ownership and `:fullscreen` rendering: if the desktop target is the video wrapper and the mobile target includes touch controls, use minimal deliberate DOM/CSS rather than fullscreening the root page and hiding many unrelated elements. Ensure WebGL overlay remains aligned to its source canvas and focus/input events continue working.
- Browser/device limitations are real: if an environment does not support arbitrary-element fullscreen, fail gracefully with brief actionable feedback and keep the normal emulator usable. Do not claim iOS Safari behavior without actual verification or silently substitute root-page fullscreen.
- Avoid creating a second emulator canvas, reinitializing Wasm/WebGL without need, adding frameworks, or changing unrelated emulator hardware behavior.

## UI principles

Follow [README UI/UX](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple**, **Show, don't tell**, **Intuitive and predictable**. The interface should explain itself by where controls are located and what Fullscreen actually does—not through extra instructional paragraphs. Retain semantic accessible labels, visible focus and a usable keyboard/tab order.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Desktop main page keeps a minimal header with snes-rust/Help/GitHub; **Scale and Display** are permanently visible in the **under-screen player controls**, with Play/Pause, Reset, volume/mute and Fullscreen grouped clearly.
- [ ] Portrait mobile and short landscape layout expose all normal controls without horizontal overflow; video and the full 12-button controller retain priority and usable touch targets. Validate tricky sizes including 320×740, 375×667, 424×320, 667×320, and relevant safe-area insets. If controls wrap, the grouping stays coherent and important messages remain reachable.
- [ ] Desktop Fullscreen enters an **actual game-only element**, with the video/CRT surface taking up as much of the viewport as the aspect ratio allows, black or neutral margins and no site header, selectors or cartridge panel. Test entry and exit by Escape and UI where appropriate.
- [ ] Touch Fullscreen shows the **live game video AND all 12 interactive SNES touch buttons** with a convenient Exit fullscreen action. Portrait and landscape controls stay visible without covering the video, and multi-touch simultaneous directions/face buttons, pointer cancellation and no-stuck-input safety remain intact.
- [ ] Keep CRT/Pixel overlay geometry exactly aligned in normal and fullscreen rendering, including 256/512 framebuffer changes, HiDPI, resizing/orientation, pausing and fullscreen exit; verify visible CRT output and correct Pixel fallback rather than relying only on selected dropdown values.
- [ ] Live Wasm game frames progress and keyboard/gamepad/touch input continues before, during and after fullscreen. No accidental pause/resume or SRAM writes/ROM reloads due solely to the fullscreen transition; mute/volume, Reset and cartridge selection still work normally after exiting.
- [ ] Update/extend real Playwright browser assertions and capture **actual** desktop, narrow portrait and short landscape screenshots before/after fullscreen for both Pixel and CRT where feasible. Verify accessible focus, an exit path on touch, unsupported Fullscreen API fallback, no visual clipping/horizontal scroll, no JS/console/CSP errors.
- [ ] Preserve legal notices in `demos/NOTICE.md`, local ROM privacy, both pinned bundled demo binaries, GitHub Pages published asset allowlist and existing browser application flows. Run the mandatory production Wasm/site build, full applicable browser tests and repo validation gates appropriate to changed files; report actual results, skips and platform limitations accurately.
- [ ] Update brief Help/README instructions only where the control placement or Fullscreen meaning changes. Avoid duplicate or stale selectors and extra compatibility scaffolding for the old root-page fullscreen behavior.

## Optional validation

Physical desktop browsers and iOS/Android devices including rotation and browser-specific fullscreen permission behavior. Useful when available, but do not require claims about devices not tested.

## Required post-merge verification

After merge, check the new `main` GitHub Pages deployment and the **live published app** with the under-screen selectors and correct fullscreen gameplay presentation on desktop/mobile viewport sizes. Record the actual run, published revision, browser evidence and any limitations. This is strictly post-merge, not a pre-merge gate. Track any confirmed regression in a separate `task` Issue when invoked; no background monitoring is implied.

## Related work

- [#162](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/162) / [PR #163](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/pull/163): moved Scale/Display out of Help into the header; this task refines placement.
- [#116](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/116): responsive full 12-button touch controls.
- [#142](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/142): Pixel/CRT display pipeline and GPU fallback.
- [#160](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/issues/160): user-controlled playback across tab switches.
